clue.text: Trivial-sounding attack rejected by doctor — it's a repetitive strain

indicators.note: -sounding attached to Trivial says the word for trivial is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: trivial matters are light ones
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for attack is read backwards

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack of illness

explanation.surface: Someone describes a medical complaint, a repetitive strain injury, dismissed by the doctor as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trivial-sounding' gives LEIT, said like LIGHT; 'rejected' turns FIT into TIF. 'Repetitive strain' misleads towards RSI: the strain is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring musical theme or phrase in an opera is literally a strain that keeps repeating.

clue.text: Wine region's traditional knowledge I concealed

indicators.note: the word for traditional knowledge conceals, or holds inside, the letter I

parts.note: lore is knowledge handed down by tradition

explanation.surface: A wine-producing area guards its old know-how jealously.
explanation.definitionFit: The valley of France's longest river is a major winemaking area, home to Sancerre and Muscadet.

clue.text: Commanding bar in America to serve fluid ounces, for example Signature

parts.note: imperial means commanding or majestic
Americans call a musical bar a measure

explanation.surface: An imposing American bar pours drinks by the fluid ounce.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bar' looks like a pub serving drinks, but it is a bar of music. 'Signature' is a stray word picked up from the page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid ounces belong to the old British system of units, alongside pints, gallons and inches.

clue.text: Insect's on a bit of log

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another comes above it

parts.note: the mantis is an insect, and its 's supplies an S

explanation.surface: An insect is perched on a piece of a log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log' looks like a piece of wood but means logarithm.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics this is the fractional part of a logarithm, as opposed to its whole-number characteristic.

clue.text: In which dancer may appear twice the same day

indicators.note: twice tells us to write the day's abbreviation two times over

parts.note: Tu is the short form of Tuesday, and the same one comes round again

explanation.surface: A dancer performs twice on one day.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina often performs wearing this short stiff skirt of layered net.

clue.text: Used washing materials in bags

definitions.meaning: wiped oneself with a face cloth, the usual British word being flannel
wearing flannel trousers, which were called bags

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means washed with a face cloth; the adjective means dressed in flannel trousers, as cricketers once were.

clue.text: Pole capturing son's heart

indicators.note: the word for pole captures the letter for son inside it

parts.note: a boom is a pole or spar on a boat
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A Polish man wins over a boy's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a spar.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is used figuratively for the heart as the seat of feelings, as in a bosom friend.

clue.text: About to fetch footloose islander -mail

indicators.note: About means going round, so the trimmed word for fetch surrounds the word to
footloose read literally means losing the foot, the last letter

parts.note: to fetch something is to bring it

explanation.surface: Someone is about to go and get a carefree inhabitant of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footloose' read literally means losing the foot, so BRIN; the trailing '-mail' is a stray scrap from the page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Britain lives on an island, so is an islander.

clue.text: Tolerating place Daisy had for dressing

parts.note: sticking means putting up with, as in can't stick it
PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Daisy put up with a place to get changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a girl's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This adhesive strip is put over a small cut, a kind of dressing for a wound.

clue.text: Composer is extremely miserable — over twelve months without a drink

indicators.note: extremely picks out the extreme letters, first and last, of miserable
without here means lacking, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: twelve months make a year
beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A composer is thoroughly unhappy after a year on the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Meyerbeer was a German-born composer of grand opera in nineteenth-century Paris.

clue.text: Impossibility of understanding what Humpty Dumpty said

definitions.meaning: the quality of being impossible to fathom
in Through the Looking-Glass Humpty Dumpty exclaims this very word to Alice

explanation.definitionFit: The word means being incomprehensible, and Lewis Carroll's egg says it in Through the Looking-Glass.

clue.text: One little creature or two that may -.be found on head

parts.note: an ear is found on the head
a wig is found on the head

explanation.surface: A tiny bug, or perhaps two, might be found on someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'found on head' serves twice: two separate things sit on the head. The '-.' before 'be' is a printing scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: This small insect with pincers at its tail is a little creature of the garden.

clue.text: Pretty girl at first working for Spectator

indicators.note: at first places the word for working before the word for pretty girl

parts.note: on means working, as a switched-on machine is
a looker is an attractive person

explanation.surface: A pretty girl started work for a magazine called the Spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectator' looks like the British weekly magazine but is just a watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking on at an event is a spectator, a watcher.

clue.text: Insect's several months on dog

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another comes above it

parts.note: spring is a season of several months
to dog someone is to tail them, follow closely

explanation.surface: An insect spends several months riding on a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal but is a verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny wingless insect leaps using a forked appendage under its body.

clue.text: As a consequence of disobedience, one gets it in the neck

definitions.text: As a consequence of disobedience, one gets it in the neck

parts.words: As a consequence of disobedience, one gets it in the neck
parts.note: reads as a punishment, but refers to the forbidden fruit in Eden that, by legend, stuck in the first man's throat as a lump

explanation.definitionFit: The bump in the throat is named after the fruit said to have lodged in Adam's throat after the Fall.

clue.text: From fearsome beast, everyone needs one sound leg-protection

parts.note: all means everyone
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sound says the word for leg-protection is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a gaiter is a covering for the lower leg

explanation.surface: Everyone needs good shin pads against a fierce animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sturdy but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alligator is leather made from the skin of the reptile, so it comes from the fearsome beast.

clue.text: Conception held in former days

indicators.note: held means contained, so the letters sit inside the word Conception

explanation.surface: An idea was entertained long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means formerly, at one time in the past.

clue.text: Breaks in new piece of military uniform

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone breaks in a new part of an army uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks in new' reads like wearing in new kit; 'new' rearranges BREAKS into BEARSK, with IN kept as it stands at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall fur cap of the Guards is part of their ceremonial military uniform.

clue.text: Weak fabric

definitions.meaning: feeble or unconvincing, as an excuse may be
a cloth woven with metallic threads, spelt with an accent

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means feeble; as a noun, a glittering cloth with gold or silver threads.

clue.text: One of ref's functions is to send off back and goalie

indicators.note: back means the word for send off is read in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to send out or off
a goalkeeper is the keeper

explanation.surface: A referee's role is to send a goalkeeper back off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send off' sounds like a red card but just means emit.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee also keeps track of the match clock, acting as official timer.

clue.text: In bad temper, having run into taxi-driver

indicators.note: into places the letter for run inside the word for taxi-driver

parts.note: a cabby drives a cab
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy after running into a cab driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable and grumpy, in a bad temper.

clue.text: What partygoers showed up in delighted the papers

parts.note: glad means delighted
rags is slang for newspapers, especially down-market ones

explanation.surface: The press was pleased to report what guests wore to the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's best clothes, worn to a party.

clue.text: Make haste eventually in old car

indicators.note: in places the final letter of haste inside the word for old car

parts.note: a crate is a slang term for an old, rickety car

indicators.note: eventually points to the end, the last letter of haste

explanation.surface: Someone finally speeds up in an old banger.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to make or bring into being.

clue.text: One ritually assumed fresh hope had died

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of hope are freshly arranged

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A fresh hope has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ritually assumed' means something put on in a ritual: assume here means don, as in clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a priestly vestment of ancient Israel, put on for ritual service.

clue.text: Dish left in cooler

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for cooler

parts.note: a fan cools the air

explanation.surface: A dish is left in the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' suggests a fridge or cool box; it is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open tart, a dish of pastry with a filling.

clue.text: Quick portrait of Tom?

parts.note: a rapid drawing, read as a picture of Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero

explanation.definitionFit: A brief rough sketch is so called; Tom Thumb's portrait would be thumbnail-sized.

clue.text: Like some pipes, but prepared to have change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart swaps the middle letter for another

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared for a change of heart, like some organ pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reed pipes in an organ, or pipes made of reed, sound reedy: thin and piping.

clue.text: Head off from valley, daring to be moved to old city

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the valley word is removed

parts.note: a glen is a Scottish valley

indicators.note: to be moved says the letters of daring are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the valley, bold enough to move to an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city of St Petersburg was named Leningrad in Soviet times.
